help.title: How it works
help.privacy: Privacy policy: camera images are processed only on your device and no data is collected ›
help.body:
1  Scan: hold one face of the cube to the camera. When the grid locks on and the outline fills up, the face is captured. Show the other faces one by one, in any order; all six are needed.

2  Check: once recognised, the whole cube is shown as a map. If the colours match, tap “Start solving”.

3  Solve: any face can point at the camera; there's no need to look for a particular colour. Instructions follow the way you hold the cube, such as “Turn the top layer left” or “Turn the right layer up”, and the small cube in the top corner is held the same way as yours. When the camera sees a move completed, the next one appears by itself; for the few moves the camera can't see, you'll be told what to do, and you can always tap “Next”.

Notation: as you hold the cube, R L U D F B are the right, left, top, bottom, front and back layers, M is the middle column and E the middle row. A plain letter means clockwise (looking at that layer), ′ means counterclockwise and 2 means a half turn.

Tips: keep your fingers off the stickers; in dim light, tap the torch at the top right.
store.name: Cube AR Solver
store.subtitle: Scan your cube, follow arrows
store.promo: Show the six faces to the camera, then follow the arrows on screen. About twenty moves later, your cube is solved.
store.description:
Cube AR Solver uses your camera to read the cube in your hands, works out a solution and then guides you, move by move, with arrows drawn right on the cube until it is solved.

SCAN
• Hold a face to the camera: the grid locks on and the outline fills up to capture it
• Scan the six faces in any order and watch the colours appear on the cube map
• Check the map before you start

FOLLOW ALONG
• Instructions follow the way you hold the cube — “Turn the top layer left”, “Turn the right layer up” — so you never hunt for a coloured face
• Arrows are drawn on the face the camera sees, and a small 3D cube shows each move
• When the camera sees a move done, the next one appears by itself; Back and Next are always there
• Spoken instructions, so your hands can stay on the cube
• Any scramble is usually solved in about 20 moves

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
• Works completely offline: recognition and solving run on your device
• Camera images are never saved or uploaded, and no data is collected
• No ads, no in-app purchases
